beats.text: Your rent has a new reported suspect. About seven billion dollars of OpenAI stock just turned into real money in staff's bank accounts.
beats.show_cue: The coverage's lead art with the OpenAI logo, then real San Francisco street footage, a steep street with Victorians.

beats.text: Here's the stupidly simple version. A tender offer is the company throwing its own staff a garage sale. Existing shares get sold to new investors, nobody waits for an IPO, and OpenAI hasn't confirmed a word of it.
beats.show_cue: An Operator-built three box diagram, staff shares to new investors to cash. Credit Bloomberg in a small text card only, it is paywalled.
curiosity_queries: Bloomberg OpenAI tender offer employee shares
private company tender offer employees explained

beats.text: One outlet ties that payout to fresh trouble in San Francisco's housing market. Reportedly is doing the heavy lifting in that sentence. Nobody's counted how many sold, or how much of it ever touched a lease.
beats.show_cue: The coverage's housing paragraph held long enough to read as one news sentence, not a finding.

San Francisco apartment listing price screenshot

beats.text: The same week, roughly 500 billion dollars was reportedly being lined up for AI data centers. Machine money and people money aren't playing the same game, and only one of them shows up on your street.
